C-PREFS-TRUTH.Summary: Config-hygiene wave 11 plus frontend findings F-004/F-011: make the preferences pipeline tell the truth end to end — validate and repair the saved profile on load (F-007), apply and clear custom CSS for real (F-001/F-011), keep theme and page-width precedence honest across a theme switch (F-002) and keep a pinned document theme off the shell (frontend F-004), align the autosave schema default with the shipped factory default (F-005), make dev:check's mode and exit status predictable (F-008/F-009), unify the two Mac App Store build profiles on one version source (F-006), and stop offering a no-op system-frame choice on Windows (F-010). One bundle because every item is a "setting does not do what the UI/doc says" defect on the same preferences/theme surface, verified against the current tree on 2026-11-21.
C-PREFS-TRUTH.Problem: Eight findings from the 2026-11-20 config-hygiene audit (score 42/100, revision 35c9223) and two from the frontend design-system audit (35/100), all re-verified in the current tree: (F-007) the prefs loader applies saved values without type or range checks — backend m005_prefs.rs declares "Schema validation is the renderer's job" (load_from, ~lines 64-115, only rejects non-object/corrupt JSON) and the renderer hydration path SET_USER_PREFERENCE (~512-528) copies any known key that is not null/undefined, so a hand-edited "autoSave": "false" (string) is truthy and enables write-through autosave (editor.js:1893 gate), and a saved autoSaveDelay of 0 reaches setTimeout raw (~1937) while the General tab range renders 1-10 seconds — the form and the timer disagree. (F-001/F-011) addCustomStyle (util/theme.js:338-342) returns early on a falsy customCss, so saving an empty value from the Custom CSS sheet (customCssSheet.vue save ~79-82, watched in app.vue:266-268) leaves the previously added style#custom-styles element live; reset has the same hole. (F-002) every theme stylesheet re-declares --editorAreaWidth (calc(100px + 768px) in all themes) and addThemeStyle mirrors those variables INLINE on document.documentElement (~219-233), which outranks the editor-width stylesheet the legacy global writer setEditorWidth writes (~290-296, fed by the editorLineWidth watcher editor.vue:1147-1151 and the Appearance text-box appearance/index.vue:74-81); reapplyLastEditorWidth (~280, pageWidth.js:323-327) restores only widths recorded by the per-document pipeline, so on a tab without a per-document entry a theme switch silently reverts the global width while the UI still shows the saved value. (F-005) the documented schema default for autoSave is false (schema.json:2-6) while preferenceDefaults() ships true (store/preferences.js:210-213, C-AUTOSAVE-DEFAULT-ON owner decision 2026-11-16) — the schema is the stale side. (F-008/F-009) tools/dev-smoke.sh takes MODE="${1:-full}" and dispatches with case --check / --quick / * (13, 124-137): any typo'd argument runs the FULL cycle, which restarts the dev server, cargo-builds and kills the running Mark process; and --check runs health_report (107-122) which prints red lines but always exits 0, so a dead server or missing Mark process reports success to the caller (package.json:35-37). (F-006) the main MAS path tools/build-mas.sh builds with --config src-tauri/tauri.mas.conf.json (line 31) which inherits version 2.8.2 from tauri.conf.json:4, while the packager hint tools/release/mas-pkg.sh:33 points at src-tauri/mas.conf.json — a stale duplicate still carrying version 2.5.0 and bundle.macOS.bundleVersion 2.5.1 (mas.conf.json:4,15) — so the two documented recipes produce different app metadata for the same revision. (F-010) Windows ships decorations:false (tauri.windows.conf.json:16) and effectiveTitleBarStyle forces 'custom' on Windows (components/titleBar/index.vue:704-714), yet the Appearance tab still offers the Custom/System select on !isOsx platforms (appearance/index.vue:110-117 with custom/native options at 269-275): on Windows the System choice is stored and silently ignored. (frontend F-004) pinning a per-document theme (editor.vue applyDocumentSurfaceTheme/applySurfaceTheme ~2754-2785) calls the same addThemeStyle used for the global theme, which repaints the whole shell — root variables, body.dark, color-scheme, native window theme — so a light document pin under global Ink flips the sidebar/title bar and the quick-settings panel dark.

Goals.Goal: F-007 — schema-validated load with repair and honest markers: the single hydration load point (ASK_FOR_USER_PREFERENCE → SET_USER_PREFERENCE) validates every key documented in _shims/preferences/schema.json against its declared type and range before it enters the store; an invalid value is repaired to the schema default (or the factory default where the schema omits one) exactly once per key, both the Settings form and the autosave timer then see the same corrected value, and each repair emits a loud BLOCK_ marker naming the key, the offending raw value and the reason. Valid profiles load byte-for-byte as today, and keys outside the documented schema are untouched.

F-001/F-011 — custom CSS empties for real: saving an empty customCss (sheet Save, reset to defaults, cross-window broadcast) clears or empties the existing style#custom-styles element so the open window immediately returns to the active theme's styles; a later non-empty save applies again. Verified for the save path and the reset path in both themes.

F-002 — one width precedence across a theme switch: after any theme application the effective --editorAreaWidth obeys the same precedence the pipeline already locks (per-document entry > global setting > theme/shipped default). Concretely: on a tab with no per-document width entry, a theme switch must not revert the saved global editorLineWidth, and the pipeline tier's reapplyLastEditorWidth behaviour for per-document widths stays exactly as shipped (document > global, both switch orders settle on the effective value).

F-005 — one autosave default: the documented schema stops contradicting the shipped behaviour — schema.json autoSave "default" becomes true, matching preferenceDefaults() (C-AUTOSAVE-DEFAULT-ON), and a consistency pin (existing preference-defaults test pattern) fails if the documented default and the factory ever drift again. No behaviour change: the factory value true and persisted-explicit-false semantics stay as shipped.

F-008/F-009 — dev:check does only what it says: tools/dev-smoke.sh dispatches explicitly — full cycle runs for the no-argument (or explicit full) invocation only; --check runs health-only; any unknown argument prints usage and exits non-zero BEFORE touching the dev server, any process or any build; and --check exits non-zero when the dev server is unreachable or the Mark process is absent, zero only when both are healthy, keeping the human-readable report.

F-006 — one MAS recipe, one version source: the two MAS instructions converge on a single build profile — the packager hint in tools/release/mas-pkg.sh points at the same config build-mas.sh uses, and the stale src-tauri/mas.conf.json is aligned to that source of truth (version inherited from tauri.conf.json; any distinct bundleVersion only if the owner keeps it, with its purpose recorded). Both documented paths then produce the same app metadata for a given revision; release-preflight's version-source cross-check stays green.

F-010 — Windows offers only what works: on Windows the title-bar-style row stops offering the system-frame option that the platform cannot honor (hidden, or disabled with an explicit why-this-is-disabled help line); the stored preference and Linux/macOS behaviour are unchanged. If the owner later approves a real Windows system frame, that is a separate change.

frontend F-004 — a pinned document theme stays on the document: the per-document theme pin applies its variables, dark classification and color-scheme to the document surface, while shared shell surfaces (file sidebar, title bar, quick-settings panel) keep following the global mode; unpinning and tab switches restore the global theme on the surface exactly as today. The pinned theme feature itself (View tab, pageWidths entry.themeOverride) is not redesigned.

Constraints.Constraint: The C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES locked model is not renegotiated: document > theme > global precedence, the single-writer rule (exactly one owner of the inline --editorAreaWidth at a time), render-time clamping with unmutated stored values, and reapplyLastEditorWidth's pipeline-tier contract stay intact; the F-002 fix extends the same precedence to the legacy global tier, it does not fork a second writer.

F-007 validation is schema-driven and conservative: only keys the documented schema declares are validated; documented legacy value forms that consumers legitimately accept (e.g. codeFontSize stored as "14px" per the C-49 contract in util/theme.js addCommonStyle) must not be "repaired"; unknown keys and session-only keys keep today's pass-through. The original file is never rewritten silently — repair is in-memory at load, persisted only when the user next saves that key.

The autosave factory default stays true; aligning the schema is a docs/schema-truth fix, not a behaviour flip. An implementation that "fixes" F-005 by changing preferenceDefaults() to false violates this spec.

tools/dev-smoke.sh keeps its three npm script entries (dev:smoke, dev:check, dev:quick) and its non-check behaviour byte-comparable; only mode dispatch, unknown-argument handling and --check exit codes change. The script stays bash, set -euo pipefail, no new dependencies.

The MAS change is metadata honesty only: no signing identity, entitlements, capability list or upload step changes; build-mas.sh keeps tauri.mas.conf.json. Removing or rewriting mas.conf.json requires the owner's confirmation recorded before merge (see CAUTION).
Every new or changed user-visible string (Windows title-bar help text, any repair notice wording) follows the ten-locale rule and the locale completeness gate.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized: file-local MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updates for touched modules (util/theme.js, util/pageWidth.js contract unchanged, store/preferences.js, tools/dev-smoke.sh markup if present, src-tauri config notes), matching graph SummaryDelta and verification entries under M-005/M-011/M-061, and START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ pairs stay unique and balanced.

NonGoals.NonGoal: F-003/F-004 of the config-hygiene audit (search maxFileSize parsing and searchExclusions enforcement in m013b/search.rs and the search stores) — a different IPC/search bundle; not touched here.
Implementing a real Windows system frame (decorations:true path, WebView2 frame styling); this bundle only removes the no-op choice.
Rearchitecting the pinned-document-theme feature, the theme family model or the quick-settings panel; F-004 scopes CSS application only.

The frontend audit's other confirmed findings (quick-settings panel clipping F-002 there, settings tab overflow F-003 there, keyboard focus F-005/F-006/F-007 there, dialog typography F-008 there, Vega test selector F-009 there, modal sheet focus trap F-010 there) — separate waves on the conveyor.
A prefs backup/restore UI or migration framework; repair-on-load is the honest minimum this bundle carries.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A profile with "autoSave": "false" (string) or autoSaveDelay 0/10001/non-number loads with each offending key repaired to its schema default, one BLOCK_ marker per repaired key naming key+reason, the Settings toggle/range and the autosave timer agreeing on the corrected values; a hand-written but valid profile loads with zero repairs and zero markers (renderer test covers both).

Saving empty CSS via the sheet and via reset both remove the stale custom layer in the open window (computed style returns to the theme value), and a subsequent non-empty save applies again (renderer test on util/theme.js addCustomStyle plus a component test for the sheet save path).

On a tab without a per-document width entry, changing the global theme keeps the saved global editorLineWidth effective (inline root value matches the global setting after the switch, both switch orders); with a per-document entry the pipeline value still wins; pageWidth unit suite stays green unchanged.
schema.json autoSave default equals preferenceDefaults().autoSave, pinned by the preference-defaults consistency test; a drift between the two fails CI.

bash tools/dev-smoke.sh --chekc (typo) prints usage and exits non-zero with no server restart, no cargo build and no kill of a running Mark (verifiable by a running sentinel process surviving); --check exits 0 only with server HTTP 200 and the process alive, non-zero on a dead server and on a missing process, each case run independently.

Both documented MAS paths reference the same config: mas-pkg.sh's missing-app hint names the profile build-mas.sh uses, mas.conf.json no longer carries a divergent version/bundleVersion (or is gone), and node tools/release-preflight.mjs passes with one coherent version source.

On Windows the title-bar-style control no longer presents System as a working choice (hidden or disabled-with-explanation); Linux and macOS rows behave exactly as before (renderer test or source pin per platform branch).

With global Ink and a light per-document pin, the document surface carries the pinned theme while sidebar/title-bar/quick-settings backgrounds follow Ink; unpin and tab-switch restore per today's contract (e2e scenario per the frontend audit's "Ограничить действие темы документа областью документа" checklist, owner-confirmed expectations).

tests/renderer/… (new/updated prefs, theme, page-width suites) and the page-width-panel e2e expectations for F-004

npm run build && npm run test:e2e (Chromium; page-width-panel scenarios for width precedence and pinned-theme shell scope)

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Green renderer suites with the new repair/clear/precedence pins; e2e width and pinned-theme scenarios green under owner-confirmed expectations; dev-smoke typo probe recorded as side-effect-free non-zero; --check negative probes recorded with non-zero exits; MAS metadata check recorded; locale gate green; no BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ pairing or unique-name regressions.

Assumptions.Assumption: All F-xx evidence lines were re-verified in the current tree on 2026-11-21 (addCustomStyle early return, editor-width mirror ordering, hydration pass-through, dev-smoke dispatch and exits, mas.conf.json 2.5.0/2.5.1, Windows forced custom frame, pinned-theme addThemeStyle reuse) — none of the six findings has been fixed by the waves merged since the audit's revision 35c9223.

AffectedAreas module ids are provisional until the authoring session freezes them from the graph: M-005 (prefs backend), M-011 (editor shell/theme/prefs UI), M-061 (width pipeline); dev-smoke and the MAS configs are script/config files without module cards.

The schema.json documented-default set is the validation scope's source of truth; where the schema and a consumer contract disagree on legacy value forms, the consumer contract wins and the key stays unvalidated until its schema entry is honest.
